**My reasoning:**

I've been farming this land in Quzhou for over 30 years. My father did the same thing, and so do all my neighbors. The land here is flat and the soil is decent - good for wheat and maize. I have about 12 mu of contracted land. My son is in Shijiazhuang now, so it's mostly me and my wife working. At my age I don't want to take risks trying something new. Wheat and maize every year, same rotation, same land - that's how it works here.

I'll plant winter wheat in October like always. I buy improved seed from the township supply co-op - Aikang 58 or whatever similar variety they have this year. The hybrid seeds for maize I buy from the same place. Been using hybrid maize for 20 years now, the yields are much better than the old ones.

For fertilizer I put down compound fertilizer at planting and then top-dress with urea when the crops need it. I probably put on a bit more than necessary but that way I know I won't fall short. The wheat needs 4 waterings - the winter watering before the ground freezes, then jointing, heading, and grain filling if it's dry. For maize I usually only need 1-2 because the summer rains help.

After I harvest the wheat in early June I need to get the maize in quickly before the rains come, so I just rotary till and seed fast. No time to do a deep plow. Spray herbicide right after for the maize, then watch for corn borers later.

I expect about 450 jin per mu for wheat and maybe 550 for maize if the weather cooperates.
